I am running a shiny app with many Hebrew characters
I have no problem seeing the hebrew or downloading Hebrew characters in an excel file or as part of a png file
the problam is that my file names are gibberish :  <http://i.stack.imgur.com/c2OkQ.png>

This is my code:
output$downloadhist <-
downloadHandler(
    filename = function() { paste(input$chosenfile,input$chosenSituation, '.png', sep="_")},
    content = function(file) {
        png(file,width     = 700,
  height    = 400,
  units     = "px",)
    print(his())
    dev.off()
  }
  )

Encoding() to the string given to filename gives: UTF-8
I tried to iconv the string to windows-1255 did nothing, tried to iconv to UTF-16 and got an error:Embedded nul in string
How can i make sure that windows can recognize the file name encoding?

messages.subject: Re: App works fine locally, but doesn't function and no error
messages.subject_clean: App works fine locally, but doesn't function and no error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,

You are my hero. The problem was that in creating the table, I used the following code for my ui:

> conditionalPanel(
> 'input.dataset === spectra.line.table',
> checkboxGroupInput('show_vars', 'Elemental lines to show:',
> names(spectra.line.table), selected = standard)
> )

And it should have been better defined, like thus:

> conditionalPanel(
> condition='input.dataset === spectra.line.table',
> checkboxGroupInput('show_vars', 'Elemental lines to show:',
> names(spectra.line.table), selected = standard)
> )

As to why this error shows up on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and not locally, I don't know, but it is up and working now. Thank you so much for taking the time to look into this issue.

---

B. Lee Drake

messages.body_plain:
Hi There,

My app works beautifully running locally or with IE, but for some plots when running on Chrome the x axis disappears.

This is what it should look like:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-DSOAI71kVkc/VrCzYbfck6I/AAAAAAAAABM/YvZwNMgebVU/s1600/local.PNG>

This is what it looks like on Chrome:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-6_xkRnSjJ14/VrCzgo9iGvI/AAAAAAAAABU/YxWU5M8STuc/s1600/Web.PNG>

Note how the x-axis is gone.

I thought perhaps it might be related to this issue <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/annotation$20missing$20on$20chrome/shiny-discuss/-9QfKodvVi0/EfGgkkI0jFgJ>, but I'm not using ggplot2, I'm using plotly (code below).

Am I doing something wrong?

thanks!

# Plot sessions with/without search
jira_average_age <- function(start_date,end_date,client,component,support_team) {

        withProgress(message = 'Processing JIRA average age', value = 0, {

                jiraData <- getCachedDatedData(start_date,end_date,getJiraDataOneDay,"jiraDataCache")

                # Remove open issues, only using closed issues for this plot
                jiraData <- jiraData[!is.na <http://is.na>(jiraData$IssueDuration),]

                # Filter our data by client, component, team
                jiraData <- filterJiraData(jiraData,client,component,support_team)

                # Extract lists for the UI
                clientList <<- sort(unique(jiraData$CustID))
                componentList <<- sort(unique(jiraData$Component))
                supportTeamList <<- sort(unique(jiraData$Assignee_Group))

                jiraData <- sqldf("select
                                    CustID,
                                    Assignee_Group,
                                    count(*) as Issues,
                                    sum(IssueDuration)/(Count(*)*1.0) as AverageAge
                                  from
                                    jiraData
                                  group by
                                    CustID,
                                    Assignee_Group
                                  order by CustID, Assignee_Group")

                # Add a left margin
                m = list(l = 150, r = 30)

                # Plotly
                f <- list(
                        family = "Courier New, monospace",
                        size = 18,
                        color = "#000000"
                )
                x <- list(
                        title = "Number of Issues",
                        titlefont = f,
                        zeroline = T,
                        zerolinecolor ='#000000',
                        zerolinewidth = 1,
                        rangemode = "tozero"
                )
                y <- list(
                        title = "Average Issue Age (days)",
                        titlefont = f,
                        zeroline = T,
                        zerolinecolor ='#000000',
                        zerolinewidth = 1,
                        rangemode = "tozero"
                )

                if(nrow(jiraData)>0) {
                   p <- plot_ly(data = jiraData, x = jiraData$Issues, y = jiraData$AverageAge, mode = "markers",
                               text=jiraData$CustID, color = jiraData$Assignee_Group) %>% layout(xaxis = x, yaxis = y, margin =m)
                } else {
                  p <- plot_ly()
                }

        })

}

(Please excuse any terrible R mistakes, only been using it, plotly and shiny for two weeks)

messages.body_plain:
There's a pull request that's somewhat stalled, here:
https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/pull/188

This is necessary in order to let you actually select points on Leaflet. Once it's merged then it would totally be possible to build these kinds of gadgets with Leaflet. You could already do one today if you wanted to where the selection was made by zooming/panning (though obviously click and drag would be nicer).

messages.subject: Re: Hide navbarmenu item?
messages.subject_clean: Hide navbarmenu item?
messages.body_plain:
You can do it, but it involves a bit of JavaScript and a basic knowledge of CSS selectors.  If you're familiar with those on a very basic level or if you're willing to put in a couple hours to learn, then you can see this StackOverflow answer to guide you:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/31703241/activate-tabpanel-from-another-tabpanel/31719425#31719425

That question deals with disabling a tab, but the solution for hiding a tab would be almost identical. It doesn't deal with menu items, but if you understand that solution then you should be able to expand on it to make it work for menu items as well. If you don't know JS or CSS at all, it might take you a bit of time and effort to understand the StackOverflow answer. Hope this helps!

ShinyURL has some bad restrictions, such as requiring you to use short variable names. It makes code maintenance harder.

messages.subject: Re: Hide navbarmenu item?
messages.subject_clean: Hide navbarmenu item?
messages.body_plain:
Actually, I just realized that hiding should be a lot easier than disabling because it doesn't require any JavaScript, you could just use `shinyjs::hide()` if you know the CSS selector of the menu item.  Ignore my previous answer, here's some code to demonstrate how to hide a tab, this is much simpler and should be fairly easy to use for menus

library(shiny)
library(shinyjs)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    useShinyjs(),
    checkboxInput("foo", "Show tab2", TRUE),
    tabsetPanel(
      id = "navbar",
      tabPanel(title = "tab1",
               value = "tab1",
               h1("Tab 1")
      ),
      tabPanel(title = "tab2",
               value = "tab2",
               h1("Tab 2")
      ),
      tabPanel(title = "tab3",
               value = "tab3",
               h1("Tab 3")
      )
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    observe({
      toggle(condition = input$foo, selector = "#navbar li a[data-value=tab2]")
    })
  }
)

messages.subject: Re: Problem with reactive environment in Shiny R
messages.subject_clean: Problem with reactive environment in Shiny R
messages.body_plain:
Any code that must be re-run when inputs change must either be in a reactive({...}) or in a renderXXX({...}). The former is for calculations that you want to use in multiple places. Each of your data frames might be one reactive. Reactives can read other reactives too, so any calculations you'll perform should also be in reactive(). Then you can refer to those reactives from your renderXXX.

Seriously though, I'd take another go through the tutorial. If these concepts aren't clear then it will be very frustrating trying to make headway with your app, but once you understand how it's supposed to work it's quite simple and elegant.

messages.subject: Some basic questions on shiny app
messages.subject_clean: Some basic questions on shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I started using shiny app just recently and have some basic questions. Any assistance is greatly appreciated.

Scenario: I have some queries that run on a database and would like to automate them so that users can request them on shiny app and it runs in the background and sends them an email with output and also highlights the updates on the main panel of which stage the process is:

####Code##########

ui.R

notes:

[I have included the necessary inputs below in ui.R and am looking for a HTML outlined box which provides updates while the process is running and gives me the output (at1.R) once its completed.

Updates like "Process started" - "First step completed" and so on]

##start

library(shiny)

# Define UI for application that draws a histogram
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  wellPanel(fluidRow(
    column(3,h1("")),column(6,h2("Title")),column(3,h1(""))
  )),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      helpText("Choose the parameters"),
      numericInput("num1", label = "Number1",value = 13342 ),
      numericInput("num2", label = "Number2", value = 1.00),
      dateRangeInput("Date1", label = "Date Range"),
      radioButtons("Ind1", label = "Indicator", choices = list("Choice" = 1, "Choice2" = 2), selected = 1),
      textInput("Username", label = "username"),
      submitButton(text = "Submit")

    )
    , mainPanel(

      htmlOutput(outputId="output")

    )

    ))

)

Server.R

library(shiny)
source('at1.R')

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

    output$output <- renderText({

      result = func(user_name = input$Username,num1 = input$num1, num2 = input$num2, date1 = input$dates[1], date2 = input$dates[2], ind1 = input$ind1)

      paste0(result)

    })

})

at1.R

This has the main R function that needs to be executed after the user submits the job. "otpt" at the end needs to be output as HTML table on to the main panel after the job is complete.

db_exec function will execute the sql on the database.

library(db)

source('ui.R')

#Provide the credentials of the database
td("xxxxxx", "xxxxxx")

#Connect to database and run a small sql
connection <- dbConnect()

Thanks in advance! Sarah

messages.subject: Export Error/Warning Messages from R console?
messages.subject_clean: Export Error/Warning Messages from R console?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe and other Shiny developers,

I have a question about how to export errors for Shiny app. Let's say I have an app doing mixed effect model, and drawing the fitted population mean plot in Shiny. When there are errors regarding the model fit (e.g., model cannot converge), we see relevant error or warning messages in R console.

However, when it comes to Shiny, there is no plot generated. We will have to go back to R console in order to check if there is something wrong, which is totally fine for developers. But for users, they may be very confused with regard to why no plot showing up in Shiny.

Therefore, is there a good way to export some error/warning messages?
(so generally, I want some 'important' error/warning messages, not ALL of them (printed in R console); In addition, we can either export the messages in Shiny or store them as a log in a temporary directory).

Any insight will be highly appreciated! Thank you.

messages.body_plain: Looks like you've got FeatureCollections inside FeatureCollections which is not valid GeoJSON AFAIK. You can use http://geojsonlint.com/ or https://github.com/ropensci/geojsonio to look into it. For the first FeatureCollection, you'll want to parse out: {"type": "FeatureCollection", "crs": { "type": "ESPG", "properties": { "code": 4326 } }, "features": [ { "properties": { "objectid": 1, "hydroid": 1, "drainid": 2, "hucid": "02020001", "name": "ags101" }, "type": "Feature", "bbox": [ -73.837555857376984, 43.95738070271539 ], "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [ -73.837555857376984, 43.95738070271539 ] } } ] } And handle the second FeatureCollection similarly (right after "feature": ). You could then pull both of these into a valid GeoJSON just by manipulating the string, or use sp (SpatialPolygonsDataFrame) + geojsonio. messages.subject: Re: Export Error/Warning Messages from R console?
messages.subject_clean: Export Error/Warning Messages from R console?
messages.body_plain:
Well an error ought to show up in Shiny, usually in bold red letters. You can try this by calling stop("boom!") from within a renderPlot, for example.

For warnings, they get printed to the console (and in Shiny server, a log file) but nothing else. You can change the handling yourself using either options(warn=[number]) to turn a warning to an error (see ?options for details) or you can use tryCatch/withCallingHandlers to do something else with warnings. http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Exceptions-Debugging.html You will still need some way of passing the message to the user; we don't have this as a feature of Shiny yet, maybe someone knows of an extension that lets you do this? Maybe in shinyjs?

messages.subject: Re: Link to send email, to attach a pdf report of output data from a calculation
messages.subject_clean: Link to send email, to attach a pdf report of output data from a calculation
messages.body_plain:
I have had good success using the mailR package (which I've tested on both gmail and MS Exchange/Outlook accounts)
(https://github.com/rpremraj/mailR)

What I do is have a button which creates a report then emails it, such as this example:

library(mailR)
library(knitr)

...

observeEvent(input$emailReport, {

  # 1) Generate the report to the working directory (or wherever you want)
  # Knit/Render your file here, or for a more basic example:
  pdf("report.pdf")
  plot(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$hp)
  dev.off()

  # 2) Email the report
  from <- [put your Outlook email acccount here]
  to <- c("per...@example.com", "per...@example.com")  # One or many recipients
  subject <- "Email Subject"
  body <- "Email body text"
  smtp <- list(host.name <http://host.name> = "smtp.office365.com <http://smtp.office365.com>", port = 587,  # If using Outlook. If not, see the link above for gmail
               user.name <http://user.name> = [your email account],
               passwd = [your password], tls = TRUE)
  files <- c("report.pdf")  # Attach the report you generated above
  send.mail(from = from, to = to, subject = subject, body = body,
                     smtp = smtp, html = TRUE, authenticate = TRUE, send = TRUE,
                     attach.files = files)
  unlink("report.pdf")  # Can optionally delete the report here when finished

})

Someone else may have a better method, but this is an example that works for me

messages.body_plain:
I'm attempting to take inputs from various sliders in a Shiny app and consolidate them into a table, however, I keep getting errors such as:

Error in UseMethod("xtable") :
no applicable method for 'xtable' applied to an object of class "c('double', numeric')"

Error in UseMethod("xtable") :
no applicable method for 'xtable' applied to an object of class "reactive"

Error in as.vector(x, mode) :
cannot coerce type 'closure' to vector of type 'any'

I've tried many ideas but cannot get it to work yet. I also haven't found any good examples or explanations to use as guide.

I just need something simple, to fill a table with the result of the sliders, and then be able to print the table via renderTable().

The code that I have that captures the input from the sliders its as follows:

sliderInput(inputId = "a.w1.a", label = "Investment on advocacy", min = 0, max = 1000000, step = 50000, value = 0),

sliderInput(inputId = "a.w1.b", label = "Investment on B", min = 0, max = 1000000, step = 50000, value = 0)

>From that, I was able to create a reactive object that then allowed me to plot successfully:

output$fund.a.w1.alloc <- reactive(input$a.w1.a + input$a.w1.b + input$a.w1.c + input$a.w1.d)

output$fund.a.w1.p <- renderPlot(barplot(d.funds.a.w1(), main = "Expenditure strategy (1000's USD)", col = "blue"))

But when I try to create a table or a matrix with that same content, I don't seem to get ir right. I have tried stuff like:

fund.w1 <- matrix(c(reactive(input$a.w1.a/1000, input$a.w1.b/1000, input$a.w1.c/1000, input$a.w1.d/1000)), nrow = 2, ncol = 2)

Or this:

fund.w1 <- reactive(matrix(c(input$a.w1.a/1000, input$a.w1.b/1000, input$a.w1.c/1000, input$a.w1.d/1000), nrow = 2, ncol = 2))

Or this:

fund.w1 <- matrix(reactive(c(input$a.w1.a/1000, input$a.w1.b/1000, input$a.w1.c/1000, input$a.w1.d/1000)), nrow = 2, ncol = 2)

I even tried to see if the data objects could compose a table by themselves, but it didn't work.

In fact, it didn't even work something as simple as:

output$fund.w1.f <- renderTable({input$a.w1.a/1000})

Or as (having created the matrix before):

fund.w1.f.test[1,1] <- renderText(input$a.w1.a)

Thank you in advanced for your help.

The current code I have replicates a similar sequence as many times as the max number of fixed stakeholders I set, leaving me with a huge 10.000 lines code that repeats continuously commands as:

tabPanel("Stakeholder #3",
fluidRow(
column(2, textInput(inputId = "sh.name.3", label = "Stakeholder's name")),
column(1),
column(4, textInput(inputId = "sh.3.option.1", label = "Option #1")),

column(4, textInput(inputId = "sh.3.option.2", label = "Option #2"))
),
fluidRow(
column(3),
column(4, textInput(inputId = "sh.3.option.3", label = "Option #3")),
column(1),
column(4, textInput(inputId = "sh.3.option.4", label = "Option #4"))
),

I'm trying to find an option that allows me to create a more compact code at the same time that provides me with a way of making a dynamic UI, which will imply the need of finding a way to be able to manage the variables dynamically as well.

Even though R naturally allows to manage variables in a very fluid way, I haven't been successful at using structures like lists, vectors or data frames in Shiny.

I checked for several days but I wasn't able to find something more elaborate than this (which has a problem with the variables resetting itself): http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/dynamic-ui.html

Is there any solution to perform something like what I am looking for?

Thank you in advanced.

messages.subject: Switching Data sets based on two user inputs
messages.subject_clean: Switching Data sets based on two user inputs
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to create an app which will show a person's stats. based on each month of the current year.  However, I am not sure how to write code that will switch data sets (ex. January data to February data) when a user selects a different month for a person.  I have tried using the switch function, but it did not switch the data when I select different months on the app.  Please see the following code:

UI R:
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(plotrix)

OpenJ16 <- read.csv("CasesOpenedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ClosedJ16 <- read.csv("CasesClosedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
CallsHandledJ16 <- read.csv("CallsHandledJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
POCJ16 <- read.csv("PercentageofCasesJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
OverJan16 <- read.csv("Overviewjan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel(title = h1("Infinite Campus Agent Stats.", align="center")),

  sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("year", "Year", c("2016")),
      br(),
      selectInput("month", "Month", c("January", "Febuary", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August","September","October","November","December")),
      br(),
      selectInput("agentNames", "Infinite Campus Agents",
                  choices = c("Andrew Davis" = 1,"Paul Dibartolo" = 2, "Michael Folan" = 3, "Megan Murray" = 4, "Victor Paulson" = 5, "Caitlin Roth" = 6)),
      br(),
      radioButtons("color", "Select Color:", choices = c("Green", "Blue", "Orange", "Red", "Yellow", "Purple"), selected = "Green")
      ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(type = "tab",
                  tabPanel("Summary",tableOutput("summaryjan16")),
                  tabPanel("Cases Open", plotOutput("janOpen16")),
                  tabPanel("Cases Closed", plotOutput("janClosed16")),
                  tabPanel("Phone Calls", plotOutput("janCH16")),
                  tabPanel("Percentage of Cases",plotOutput("janPC16"),br(),plotOutput("janPC216"))

      )
    )

    )
  )
)

Server R:
library(shiny)
library(plotrix)

OpenJ16 <- read.csv("CasesOpenedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ClosedJ16 <- read.csv("CasesClosedJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
CallsHandledJ16 <- read.csv("CallsHandledJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
POCJ16 <- read.csv("PercentageofCasesJan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
OverJan16 <- read.csv("Overviewjan16.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

shinyServer(
  function(input, output, session)
  {
    output$janOpen16 <- renderPlot({
      colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
      barplot(OpenJ[,colm],breaks=seq(0, max(Open[,colm])), col = input$color, main = "Cases Opened in January", xlab = names(Open[colm]), ylab = "Cases Opened",names.arg = c("01/04","01/11","01/18","01/24"))
    })

    output$janCH16 <- renderPlot({
      colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
      plot(CallsHandledJ[,colm],type = "l",lwd=2, col = input$color,xlab = names(CallsHandledJ[colm]), ylab = "Calls Handled in January", main = "Calls Handled in January",ylim = c(0,40))
    })

  output$janClosed16 <- renderPlot({
    colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
    barplot(ClosedJ[,colm],breaks=seq(0, max(Open[,colm])), col = input$color, main = "Cases Closed in January", xlab = names(Open[colm]), ylab = "Cases Closed",names.arg = c("01/04","01/11","01/18","01/24"))
  })

  output$janPC16 <- renderPlot({
    colm <- as.numeric(input$agentNames)
    pie3D(POCJ16[,colm],labels = names(Open[colm]),explode = 0.1, main = "Percentage of Cases Picked Up")
  })

  output$janPC216 <- renderPlot({
    pc <- c(22.6,10.16,20.11,13.57,9.78,22.25)
    lbls <- c("Andrew Davis","Paul DiBartolo","Michael Folan","Megan Murray","Victor Paulson","Caitlin Roth")
    pct <- round(pc/sum(pc)*100)
    lbls <- paste(lbls, pct)
    lbls <- paste(lbls,"%",sep="")
    pie(pc, labels = lbls, main = "Percentage of Cases Picked Up",col = rainbow(length(lbls)))
  })

  output$summaryjan16 <- renderTable(OverJan16)
    }
)

For example, when we create uiOutput(s) for users to select variables, I notice that there is often an error message saying 'Error: undefined columns selected' (before this variable gets selected). We do NOT want this type of error to show up to users; rather, we just want to show the modeling errors. I know that we can completely turn off error messages by specifying
tags$style(type = "text/css",
           ".shiny-output-error { visibility: hidden; }",
           ".shiny-output-error:before { visibility: hidden; }")

This will suppress ALL the error messages including any possible ones from modeling/analysis. Therefore, I wonder is there a way to control which error messages to show, and which to not show? Or alternatively, turn off error message for some pages, but turn it back on when needed (like, .shiny-output-error {visibility: show;} or something similar)?

Sorry if this question seems to be dumb. but yea thank you so much!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Let's try.

This is the code in my server.R

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(tree)
library(tidyr)

# Reads data frames

sergio_train_plot <- readRDS("data/sergio_train_plot.RDS")
sergio_test_plot <- readRDS("data/sergio_test_plot.RDS")

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

# Choses one dataframe according to a selectInput in ui.R

  data_plot <- reactive({
    switch(input$user,
           "Sergio (train)" = sergio_train_plot,
           "Sergio (test)" = sergio_test_plot
                   )
  })

 # Creates a reactive slider that lets the user to choose max and min datetimes to plot

  output$reacSlider <- renderUI({
    mindate = min(round.POSIXt(data_plot()$datetime - 30*60, "hour"))
    maxdate = max(round.POSIXt(data_plot()$datetime + 30*60, "hour"))
    sliderInput("periodo", "Periodo",
                min = mindate , max = maxdate,
                value = c(mindate, maxdate),
                step = 3600,
                width = "80%")
  })

  time_margins <- reactive({
    input$periodo
  })

  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    t1 <- time_margins()[1]
    t2 <- time_margins()[2]
    plot_dataset <- data_plot()
    dataset1 <- plot_dataset[plot_dataset$datetime > t1 & plot_dataset$datetime < t2,]
    ggplot(data = dataset1) +
      geom_line(aes(x = datetime, y = rssi, colour = wp), size=.5) +
      ylim(-100, -20) +
      theme(plot.title=element_text(vjust = -2.5)) +
      theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
            axis.title.y=element_blank()) +
      labs(colour="Wall Plug:") +
      geom_rect(aes(xmin=datetime-30, xmax=datetime+30, ymin=-100, ymax=-97, fill=factor(patron))) +
      labs(fill="Patrón:")# +      scale_fill_discrete(labels=c(1:12))
    })

  output$plot2 <- renderPlot({
    t1 <- time_margins()[1]
    t2 <- time_margins()[2]
    plot_dataset <- data_plot()
    dataset1 <- plot_dataset[plot_dataset$datetime > t1 & plot_dataset$datetime < t2,]
    ggplot(data = dataset1) +
      geom_line(aes(x = datetime, y = rssi, colour = wp), size=.5) +
      ylim(-100, -20) +
      theme(plot.title=element_text(vjust = -2.5)) +
      theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
            axis.title.y=element_blank()) +
      labs(colour="Wall Plug:") +
      geom_rect(aes(xmin=datetime-30, xmax=datetime+30, ymin=-100, ymax=-97, fill=factor(prediccion))) +
      labs(fill="Predicción")
  })

})

And this is the ui.R code

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel(h1("Calibración de sensores por patrones")),

  fluidRow(
    column(12,
           h2("Control")
    ),

    column(2,
      selectInput("user", "Usuario", c("Sergio (train)", "Sergio (test)"))
    ),

    column(9, offset = 1,
      uiOutput("reacSlider")
    )
  ),

  fluidRow(
    column(12,

      h2("Resultados"),
      plotOutput("plot1"),
      plotOutput("plot2")

    )
  )

))

Thanks for your help

messages.subject: Re: Export Error/Warning Messages from R console?
messages.subject_clean: Export Error/Warning Messages from R console?
messages.body_plain:
You shouldn't ignore those warnings, but rather endeavor to make them go away. In the case of missing inputs, use the req() function to abort processing cleanly: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html

On Mon, Feb 8, 2016 at 8:31 AM YL <liy...@gene.com> wrote:

> Hi Joe,
>
> Thank you for your reply.
>
> I understand that any error messages will show up in Shiny (in bold red letters). However, some of them are not of interest. For example, when we create uiOutput(s) for users to select variables, I notice that there is often an error message saying 'Error: undefined columns selected' (before this variable gets selected). We do NOT want this type of error to show up to users; rather, we just want to show the modeling errors. I know that we can completely turn off error messages by specifying
> tags$style(type = "text/css",
>            ".shiny-output-error { visibility: hidden; }",
>            ".shiny-output-error:before { visibility: hidden; }")
>
> This will suppress ALL the error messages including any possible ones from modeling/analysis. Therefore, I wonder is there a way to control which error messages to show, and which to not show? Or alternatively, turn off error message for some pages, but turn it back on when needed (like, .shiny-output-error {visibility: show;} or something similar)?
>
> Sorry if this question seems to be dumb. but yea thank you so much!
>
>
> On Friday, February 5, 2016 at 2:47:45 PM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > Well an error ought to show up in Shiny, usually in bold red letters. You can try this by calling stop("boom!") from within a renderPlot, for example.
> >
> > For warnings, they get printed to the console (and in Shiny server, a log file) but nothing else. You can change the handling yourself using either options(warn=[number]) to turn a warning to an error (see ?options for details) or you can use tryCatch/withCallingHandlers to do something else with warnings. http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Exceptions-Debugging.html You will still need some way of passing the message to the user; we don't have this as a feature of Shiny yet, maybe someone knows of an extension that lets you do this? Maybe in shinyjs?
> >
> > On Fri, Feb 5, 2016 at 8:11 AM YL <liy...@gene.com> wrote:
> > > Hi Joe and other Shiny developers,
> > >
> > > I have a question about how to export errors for Shiny app. Let's say I have an app doing mixed effect model, and drawing the fitted population mean plot in Shiny. When there are errors regarding the model fit (e.g., model cannot converge), we see relevant error or warning messages in R console.
> > >
> > > However, when it comes to Shiny, there is no plot generated. We will have to go back to R console in order to check if there is something wrong, which is totally fine for developers. But for users, they may be very confused with regard to why no plot showing up in Shiny.
> > >
> > > Therefore, is there a good way to export some error/warning messages?
> > > (so generally, I want some 'important' error/warning messages, not ALL of them (printed in R console); In addition, we can either export the messages in Shiny or store them as a log in a temporary directory).
> > >
> > > Any insight will be highly appreciated! Thank you.

messages.subject: Problem with dateRangeInput

messages.body_plain:
Hi
I am new in R shiny. I have created a script using "dateRangeInput". It works fine. However, when I am trying to change the time, script starts running before changing both start and end time and giving some error/warning messages because of the bad time values. At the end, it gives right plot. Any idea to get rid off this problem. Here is the few necessary lines from ui.R and server.r.

ui.R

dateRangeInput("dates",
               "Date range",
               start = "1988-01-01",
               #end = as.character(Sys.Date())),
               end = "2010-12-31",
               min    = "1988-01-01",
               max    = "2010-12-31",
               separator = " - ")

server.R

x1 <- as.numeric(gsub("-", "", input$dates[1]))*100
x2 <- as.numeric(gsub("-", "", input$dates[2]))*100

W.df = subset(obsc.datain_short,date>= x1 & date<x2)

with regards
-Deb

messages.subject: subsetting a dataset through dropdown input, and excluding some points in interactive plot
messages.subject_clean: subsetting a dataset through dropdown input, and excluding some points in interactive plot
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I tried to realize/implement a combination of two main features in a shiny application. My dataset contains several columns, some of those columns are values measured in categorical type, like locations and professions, some columns are numeric type values. I want to combine the two major features below,

first, provide a dropdown/selectInput in  user interface that enables users to select a certain subset of the whole dataset. For instance, the choices available in one dropdown could be the locations in the location column: all distinct locations in the dataset. When users switch from one choice／location to another, the serve side switch from one subset to another subset. Therefore, it can be viewed as dynamic subsetting.

Second, after selecting a certain subset,  users select two numeric columns to generate a scatterplot. A regression/trend line will be generated based on such a cloud points, using ggplot, ggsmooth, function to generate the trend line. And a range is generated around the regression pattern. For instance, to estimate the wage of a certain profession in a certain location, we calculate both a point estimate and a range estimate. The plot is interactive in that, when users click some points in the scatterplot, those points being clicked will be excluded in the calculation of regression/trend line. When excluded, the points become grey in colour from dark black colour. The reason why excluding some points is that users can view certain points as outliers, and tag them as not usable in regression analysis. Users can see how the selection or exclusion of certain points impact the estimated trend line and range estimates.

The existing R scripts for the exlusion of data points through mouse clicks is displayed in the following webaddress.

http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/plot-interaction-exclude.html

I have realized features like dynamic subsetting alone and point exclusion under a static dataset. But I failed to combine them both into a single shiny app.

messages.subject_clean: Scatterplot Exclusion in Shiny Module
messages.body_plain:
I am having issues with recreating the example at the link below in regards to having a scatter where points can be excluded. I am trying to do this inside a Shiny module. Below is the reproducible example...

I keep getting the following message:
"Error in $<-.data.frame: replacement has 0 rows, data has 32"
66: $<-.data.frame
65: $<-
64: brushedPoints
63: observeEventHandler [/app.R#64]
1: shiny::runApp

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

###### SCATTER GRAPHS ###############
scatter_graphUI <- function(id, tab_panel_name, height = "500px") {
  ns <- NS(id)

  tabPanel(tab_panel_name,
           plotOutput(ns("scatter_1"), height = height, click = ns("plot1_click"), brush =
                        brushOpts(id = ns("plot1_brush"))),
           actionButton(ns("exclude_toggle"), "Toggle points"),
           actionButton(ns("exclude_reset"), "Reset")
  )
}

scatter_graph <- function(input, output, session, scatter_data, col_select) {

  vals <- reactiveValues()
  data_df <- reactive({
    scatter_df <- scatter_data()
    main_df <- scatter_df[,col_select]
    vals$keeprows = rep(TRUE, nrow(main_df))
    main_df
  })

  output$scatter_1 <- renderPlot({

    graph_df <- data_df()
    # Plot the kept and excluded points as two separate data sets
    keep    <- graph_df[vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]
    exclude <- graph_df[vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]

    final_df <- keep
    title = paste(colnames(final_df)[1], "vs", colnames(final_df)[2])
    axis_text = 12
    title_text = 16

    # create a generic graphing final_df
    colnames(final_df) <- c("xaxis","yaxis")
    colnames(exclude) <- c("xaxis","yaxis")

    # setup the graph
    gg <- ggplot(final_df, aes(x = xaxis, y = yaxis)) + geom_point()
    gg <- gg + geom_point(data = exclude, fill = NA, color = "black", alpha = 0.25)
    gg <- gg + stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), size = 1)
    gg <- gg + theme_bw()
    gg
  })

  # Toggle points that are clicked
  observeEvent(input$plot1_click, {
    main_df <- data_df()
    res <- nearPoints(main_df, input$plot1_click, allRows = TRUE)
    vals$keeprows <- xor(vals$keeprows, res$selected_)
  })

  # Toggle points that are brushed, when button is clicked
  observeEvent(input$exclude_toggle, {
    main_df <- data_df()
    res <- brushedPoints(main_df, input$plot1_brush, allRows = TRUE)
    vals$keeprows <- xor(vals$keeprows, res$selected_)
  })

  # Reset all points
  observeEvent(input$exclude_reset, {
    main_df <- data_df()
    vals$keeprows <- rep(TRUE, nrow(main_df))
  })

}
########################################

header <- dashboardHeader(
  title = 'Test Dashboard'
)
body <- dashboardBody(
  tabItems(
    tabItem(tabName = "scatter_eval",
            tabBox(
              title = "Scatter",
              selected = "Selected",
              height = "600px", side = "right",
              scatter_graphUI("selected_scatter", "Selected")
            )
    )
  )
)

sidebar <- dashboardSidebar(
  sidebarMenu(
    menuItem("Scatter Evaluation", icon = icon("th"), tabName = "scatter_eval")
  )
)

ui <- dashboardPage(skin = "blue",
                    header,
                    sidebar,
                    body
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  callModule(scatter_graph, id ="selected_scatter", scatter_data = reactive(mtcars),
             col_select = c(1,2))

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: How to build an R package based on a shiny application
messages.subject_clean: How to build an R package based on a shiny application
messages.body_plain:
You need to create a shiny "app object" from within your package. You can either do this directly inside your function like this:

launchApp <- function() {
  ui <- fluidPage(...)
  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    ...
  }
  app <- shinyApp(ui, server)
  runApp(app)
}

Or if your app is bundled as .R files in your package, e.g. under inst/shiny/app1, you'd do something like this:

launchApp <- function() {
  app <- shinyAppDir(system.file("shiny/app1", package="mypackage"))
  runApp(app)
}

messages.subject: Re: caching issues
messages.subject_clean: caching issues
messages.body_plain:
While your shiny server function is run every time a new browser connects, the server.R file itself is only evaluated 1) when that particular R process first starts up, and 2) when server.R is modified and then a new browser connects. There are a couple of ways you can get the behavior you want.

Option 1: The cron job that does the work can do "touch restart.txt" in the Shiny app directory when it's done. This will force Shiny Server to start a new R process and retire the old one when the next browser arrives.

Option 2: Keep the cron job the way it is, but use reactiveFileReader <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/reactiveFileReader.html> to create auto-updating versions. This would mean even browsers that are already showing the old data, would automatically update themselves when new data arrives, without needing to reload. You can put the reactiveFileReaders above the shiny server function if the same data is to be shared by everyone.

messages.subject: reduce rate of plot redraws or ignore numeric spinner until released
messages.subject_clean: reduce rate of plot redraws or ignore numeric spinner until released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This is pretty much a question I've just asked on the coursera data products course, but I thought I might have a better chance of an answer here.

I have a plot in a shiny app that takes a little while to redraw, it's <1s, but a noticeable time. This plot is dependent on some numeric input values. If you adjust these by holding down the spinner (up/down) buttons it looks like flushes build up for each value you go through. This means when you release the button the plot continues to redraw itself, apparently going through each value that the numeric input did. Responsiveness not great...

Roughly:
mydata <- reactive({myfunction(myinput(), input$value, ...)})
myplot <- reactive({
    localdata <- mydata()
    #... do stuff to localdata
    qplot(xval,yval,data=localdata)
})
output$outplot <- renderPlot({myplot()})

There are other dependencies in there, but this is the only place input$value appears. I've tried various things with isolate() and priorities, but can't stop it happening (unless myplot is never updated). I don't want the plot to update until the spinner is released, it should redraw only once. Any idea how to do that? I know a separate 'update' button is an option, but would like to try to avoid it. Been looking at suspend, but don't think it will help. The right solution would probably be to only fire the flush on release of the spinner button, but that would require customisation of the input element. I've been wondering if an invalidateLater observer that updates a reactiveValues object with the input values when they change would work to insulate the plot from individual updates and allow me to control the redraw frequency without forcing a redraw every n seconds. Alternatively, any way to drop new flushes for a dead period after a redraw (ideally while redrawing once at the end of that period)?

Thanks for your time.

--

imalone

messages.body_plain:
You're right that letting you customize the debounce/throttle rate of the spinner would be the best solution. In the meantime, take a look at this gist: https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/6141ea7066e62cafb31c

You can copy that code into your server.R or global.R, and then use it to wrap the input$value. For example:

debouncedValue <- debounce({input$value}, 500)
mydata <- reactive({myfunction(myinput(), debouncedValue(), ...)})

This will prevent changes from input$value to propagate through debouncedValue until input$value has stopped changing for approximately 500 milliseconds.

messages.subject: Re: Unused Arguments
messages.subject_clean: Unused Arguments
messages.body_plain:
This shouldn't be a reactive expression at all, then. You want to do this:

observeEvent(input$ssrVerify, {

       f1 <- filedata1()
       f2 <- filedata2()
       #if(is.null(f1)) return(NULL)
       #if(is.null(f2)) return(NULL)
       ssrVerify(f1,f2)
})

Writing to disk is an action not a calculation. If you want to perform an action, use observe or observeEvent. If you want to do a calculation (i.e. return a value) and there are no side effects like writing to disk, that's the right time to use reactive or eventReactive.

If you're wondering where this little bit of advice is documented, unfortunately, it's not--we're working on it now, though.

messages.subject: Faster Javascript Charting Libraries
messages.subject_clean: Faster Javascript Charting Libraries
messages.body_plain:
I have a Shiny app which pulls in around 250k records, all of which are currently displayed in a ggplot line chart. This chart takes several seconds to display, after the rest of the app has finished loading.

About 18 months ago, I ran some tests with various javascript charting libraries, with R bindings - rCharts, Plotly, GoogleVis. They were all slower than ggplot to display chart results.

I decided I could live without the interactivity, in exchange for faster load times.

Over the last 12 months there has been a lot of advances in htmlwidgets for R and many more bindings to javascript libraries. I do currently use the very nice MetricsGraphics htmlwidgets (http://hrbrmstr.github.io/metricsgraphics/) interface to display scatter plots, for smaller, subsetted data.

Has anyone undertaken research as to whether some of these javascript library bindings are as fast or faster than ggplot? I'm guessing the answer is that they won't be faster, but as things have moved on since last I looked, I thought it worth asking.

messages.body_plain:
In server.R use input$month with an "if" statement:

if(input$month == "January") {

dataSet <- read.csv(CasesOpenedJan16.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

} else if (input$month == "February") {

dataSet <- read.csv(CasesOpenedFeb16.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

} else if (input$month %in% c("March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December") == TRUE) {

dataSet <- paste("You can't time travel to the future")

}

The variable dataSet will then be changed based on the selected value of input$month.

I also don't think you need to load the csv files in ui.R. It'll save some time if you don't.

messages.body_plain:
Maybe output the value of the system() call from within shinyServer() to an Rds file. Then load the Rds file from a separate R script, but include the R script as a source in server.R

Without actually writing the code.....

1. Output value of system() call, found within shinyServer(), to an Rds file.
2. R script called system.R loads the Rds file and saves the value to a variable.
3. In server.R "source" system.R, but outside of shinyServer() function:

source("system.R", local=TRUE)

This should execute the code found in system.R, and make the variable containing Rds/system() data available.

If feels a bit clunky, but I think it should work.

messages.subject: Using dynamic UI components when using Shiny modules
messages.subject_clean: Using dynamic UI components when using Shiny modules
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

We're using Shiny modules quite extensively and love it. There's one specific issue that we're running into.

We have a Shiny app with several modules. Most of them are independent of each other but one is a special case of a 'nested' model (which isn't really nested). The situation is as follows: we have a tab with specific set of inputs and outputs. Given the structure of our layout, we are not able to render the inputs of the tab in the UI function of the tab itself. All of the inputs are in a separate filter module that renders the filters for a given tab depending on which tab is selected. This works perfectly, and allows us in the server part of a tab component to take dependencies on inputs as if they were shown by the UI function of that tab.

The issue is that we need dynamic UI components where it's impossible or very inefficient to use for example updateSelectInput. This means that certain inputs in the exported UI have to be dependent on inputs from the same exported UI. This does not work. It only works if we split up the exported UI into several renderUI parts. The issue with this is that our filters are different across tabs so that rendering the UI in the filter module become really tedious if we have to handle a dynamic number of renderUI components.

I'm sure that this is all very confusing so I've put together three examples. Please see https://gist.github.com/Vestaxis/8a785b63c7b4566a2954.

Any input would be greatly appeciated.

messages.subject: rsession-ld-library-path equivalent for Shiny-Server?
messages.subject_clean: rsession-ld-library-path equivalent for Shiny-Server?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

One of my shiny apps relies on an R package that uses an external library outside of the standard R library search paths.

If I open a standard R session and load the package on my Ubuntu Server (14.04) everything works, the package loads and the functions produce results.

When I tried the same thing via RStudio Server I got this error message:

Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
unable to load shared object '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/gurobi/libs/gurobi.so': libgurobi65.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

I was able to resolve this problem by following the recommendation here: http://www.gurobi.com/documentation/6.5/quickstart_linux/r_installing_the_r_package.html

If you are using R from RStudio Server, and you get an error indicating that R is unable to load the Gurobi DLL or shared object, you may need to set the rsession-ld-library-path entry in the server config file. Please consult the RStudio documentation for more information.

So I set rsession-ld-library-path to the appropriate path and the package works from RStudio Server as well. If I start my Shiny app from within RStudio Server it works too.

If I use Shiny-Server I get the same error message as above (all my other Shiny apps work fine). Now I am wondering if there is an equivalent to rsession-ld-library-path for Shiny-Server or if I am missing something else here that Shiny is doing?

messages.subject: Re: Using dynamic UI components when using Shiny modules
messages.subject_clean: Using dynamic UI components when using Shiny modules
messages.body_plain:
I don't think I'm going to articulate this well, but I'll try:

In your examples, you're splitting the uiOutput and the renderUI calls across distinct modules. That's something you don't want to do. Instead, endeavor to keep the uiOutput and renderUI defined in the same module.

The way you should inject one module A's UI into another module B's UI, is by actually passing tag objects (created by module A's UI function) into the B UI function. In other words, the actual uiOutput should belong to the "tab" module.

But there's already a tabUI function that has textOutput in it, and that needs to render somewhere different than inside the tab. How can you let a module put UI in two places on the page (one wherever the textOutput needs to go, and one inside the filter UI)? You can either split the module into two modules (and have them communicate through reactive expressions), or... you can have multiple UI functions for a single module! I've taken this latter approach in the gist below, where I updated all three of your examples:

https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/4bdd7ba0f84580f37e91

It's OK to have an n-to-1 relationship between UI functions and module server functions. Just make sure that all the UI functions for a given module instance are invoked with the same id, as I do in the gist.

On Fri, Feb 12, 2016 at 6:37 AM Niels Schenk <ni...@increaseonline.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> We're using Shiny modules quite extensively and love it. There's one specific issue that we're running into.
>
> We have a Shiny app with several modules. Most of them are independent of each other but one is a special case of a 'nested' model (which isn't really nested). The situation is as follows: we have a tab with specific set of inputs and outputs. Given the structure of our layout, we are not able to render the inputs of the tab in the UI function of the tab itself. All of the inputs are in a separate filter module that renders the filters for a given tab depending on which tab is selected. This works perfectly, and allows us in the server part of a tab component to take dependencies on inputs as if they were shown by the UI function of that tab.
>
> The issue is that we need dynamic UI components where it's impossible or very inefficient to use for example updateSelectInput. This means that certain inputs in the exported UI have to be dependent on inputs from the same exported UI. This does not work. It only works if we split up the exported UI into several renderUI parts. The issue with this is that our filters are different across tabs so that rendering the UI in the filter module become really tedious if we have to handle a dynamic number of renderUI components.
>
> I'm sure that this is all very confusing so I've put together three examples. Please see https://gist.github.com/Vestaxis/8a785b63c7b4566a2954.
>
> Any input would be greatly appeciated.

 D3TableFilter supports paging (client side only, not server side like DT). More important though, performance for a few hundred rows should be no problem. Best

Thomas

messages.subject: Sending data from JS to SHINY
messages.subject_clean: Sending data from JS to SHINY
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for releasing the new shiny 13.0 and including JS Events in the new version. Very helpful :) Beautiful what you did to debugg reactive apps btw. :)

However, I wonder if there is any way to send data from JS back to shiny/R?
As described http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/js-events.html it seems that this is a one way street. Only data from Shiny can be send to JS, but not back. What if I need data that is created in JS in my shiny/R Application for further process? There still is this undocumented feature https://ryouready.wordpress.com/2013/11/20/sending-data-from-client-to-server-and-back-using-shiny/ which works. However, did you include a way to send data from JS back to shiny?

messages.subject: Re: Sending data from JS to SHINY
messages.subject_clean: Sending data from JS to SHINY
messages.body_plain:
To send data from JS to Shiny, you need a shiny container, like textInput, and then you need write some js script like:

var x = "Hello world!"
var tar = $("#id")  // where the id is the id of a textInput of your shiny-app.
tar.val(x)
tar.trigger("change")

I suppose you know how to programme with JS.

What I need is to access a dataframe that gets created in Shiny. Is that possible with the new features?!

messages.body_plain:
A function I have in my Shiny app requires passing a character symbol that uses backslashes in R. For example, my R program is similar to

myFun <- foo(arg1, arg2 = '\n')

In Shiny, I use textInput for arg2 as this character must allowed to be any possible character the user would need to pass to this function.

However, using textInput to send '\n" actually sends '\\n" to the function. Perhaps an easy way to see this is to use the existing example at the link below and type in text into the textInput example.

http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/widget-gallery.html

Is there a way to enter text into textInput such that it passes *only* '\n'?

Thank you

Thanks, Joe! I really appreciate your help, and your great contribution to the community!

I have not done any javascript before and got some time over the weekend to read some basics about it.

Here is the code snippet that seems to do the job :

Replacing this line:

          actionButton("action1","Submit")

with :

              tags$button("Submit",id="myButton",type="button"),
              tags$script('
                document.getElementById("myButton").onclick = function() {
                  var sure= confirm("Are you sure to submit?");
                  if (sure) {
                    # change it to a random number to trigger the send from ui.R to server.R
                    # as static value is not going to be sent
                    var randomNumber=Math.random();
                    Shiny.onInputChange("action1", randomNumber);
                  } else {
                    Shiny.onInputChange("action1", sure);
                  }
                };
              ')

It seems to work, but there is likely other ways that work better. I am all ears if any one wants to chime in!

messages.body_plain:
Is there a way to stop something from running or updating when a button is pressed? The example I have in mind is a button that adds residuals or predictions from a regression to a dataset. The variable is added and, even though the selection of variables in the model doesn't change, the model is re-estimated because the data changed. This is not a big deal when the data is small but when it gets larger ...

Of course, usually you do want the model to be re-estimated when the data changes. However, when the add-prediction button is pressed i'd like this **not** to happen. Seems like the opposite of what req does. Is there a way to do something like this?

messages.subject_clean: ggplot + brushedPoints needs xvar=xxx, yvar=yyy when aes(color=zzz)
messages.body_plain:
I found that the problem was not with aes(color=) but location of aes() in general.  I removed aes(color=) but if I put aes(x=xxx, y=yyy) outside of ggplot() or geom_point(), mouse interaction fails, as the code shown below.  If you move 'aes(x=wt, y=mpg)' into either ggplot() or geom_point(), it works.

Also, keeping the aes() outside location but adding xvar='wt', yvar='mpg' to brushedPoints and nearPoints will fix the problem, too!

 Must be a bug?

=========================
library(ggplot2)
library(shiny)

ui <- basicPage(
  plotOutput("plot1", brush = "plot_brush", click = "plot_click", height = 250),
  verbatimTextOutput("info"),
  verbatimTextOutput("info2")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
     ggplot(mtcars) + aes(x=wt, y=mpg) + geom_point() +
      facet_grid(. ~ cyl) +
      theme_bw()
  })

  output$info <- renderPrint({
    brushedPoints(mtcars, input$plot_brush)
  })

  output$info2 <- renderPrint({
    nearPoints(mtcars, input$plot_click)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Recommended way to create dynamic number of observers?
messages.subject_clean: Recommended way to create dynamic number of observers?
messages.body_plain:
Interesting question. I'm not sure there is a 'good' answer but one thing you could do to avoid multiple observers linked to the same button is to name them and then suspend them as needed when the numeric input changes. Perhaps better, if the observers are named I expect you you can check if one already exists for that button and only create new ones as needed (or delete/suspend ones that are no longer needed).

On Saturday, February 13, 2016 at 12:51:45 AM UTC-8, Dean Attali wrote:
> I've seen similar questions in the past but I haven't seen a satisfactory answer.
>
> To demonstrate, imagine this simple toy app:  There's a numeric input that lets the user decide how many buttons there will be on the page.  Clicking on each button should print out the number of that button.
>
> Here's the "best naive" implementation I could think of:
>
> library(shiny)
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   numericInput("num", "Number of buttons", 3),
>   uiOutput("buttons")
> )
>
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   output$buttons <- renderUI({
>     lapply(seq_len(input$num), function(x) {
>       actionButton(paste0("btn", x), x)
>     })
>   })
>
>   observe({
>     lapply(seq_len(input$num), function(x) {
>       observeEvent(
>         input[[paste0("btn", x)]],
>         cat(x)
>       )
>     })
>   })
> }
>
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
>
> This isn't ideal for two reason: first of all, it seems weird to me to have an observer within an observe.  Is that ok to do?  Second, every time the loop runs, ALL the previous observers that existed get duplicated. For example, if the app starts and we click on the button "2" then the number "2" will get printed once.  But if we change the number of buttons, and then change it again, then that loop will be called two more times, and now there are three observers for the "2" button, so clicking "2" will print it 3 times.
>
> I hope that's clear enough.  Obviously my use cases are more realistic than this, but this seems simple enough to understand
>
> Another approach would be to just pick a very large number and loop once to create a lot of observers, but that's not ideal either.

messages.subject: Show empty plot while execution is going on
messages.subject_clean: Show empty plot while execution is going on
messages.body_plain:
I am using progress bar in shiny when heavy execution is going on. It works great. The problem is when input value changes, previous plot (with previous input) is shown unless required plot is ready . Is there a way that during execution time, i can print any message or as another option plot output can be shown empty. I dont want plot of previous input to be shown while waiting. As my code is very long, i have prepared an example here. any help will be really appreciated.
ui.r
shinyUI(bootstrapPage(

  selectInput(inputId = "n_breaks",
              label = "Number of bins in histogram (approximate):",
              choices = c(10, 20, 35, 50),
              selected = 20),

  checkboxInput(inputId = "individual_obs",
                label = strong("Show individual observations"),
                value = FALSE),

  checkboxInput(inputId = "density",
                label = strong("Show density estimate"),
                value = FALSE),

  plotOutput(outputId = "main_plot", height = "300px"),

  # Display this only if the density is shown
  conditionalPanel(condition = "input.density == true",
                   sliderInput(inputId = "bw_adjust",
                               label = "Bandwidth adjustment:",
                               min = 0.2, max = 2, value = 1, step = 0.2)
  )

))

server.r
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$main_plot <- renderPlot({
    withProgress(message = 'Calculation in progress',
                 detail = 'This may take a while...', value = 0,
                 {

                   for (i in 1:10) {
                     incProgress(1/30)
                     Sys.sleep(0.25)
                   }
    hist(faithful$eruptions,
         probability = TRUE,
         breaks = as.numeric(input$n_breaks),
         xlab = "Duration (minutes)",
         main = "Geyser eruption duration")

    if (input$individual_obs) {
      rug(faithful$eruptions)
    }

    if (input$density) {
      dens <- density(faithful$eruptions,
                      adjust = input$bw_adjust)
      lines(dens, col = "blue")
    }
                 })

  })
})

You need a reactive expression to represent the subsetted data.

subsetted <- reactive({
  dF %>%
    filter(rank >= input$impact[1] & rank <= input$impact[2]) %>%
    filter(class == input$method)
})

Then, the first argument to ggplot() needs to change from `dF` to `subsetted()`.

On Thu, Feb 11, 2016 at 11:38 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> While your shiny server function is run every time a new browser connects, the server.R file itself is only evaluated 1) when that particular R process first starts up, and 2) when server.R is modified and then a new browser connects. There are a couple of ways you can get the behavior you want.
>
> Option 1: The cron job that does the work can do "touch restart.txt" in the Shiny app directory when it's done. This will force Shiny Server to start a new R process and retire the old one when the next browser arrives.
>
> Option 2: Keep the cron job the way it is, but use reactiveFileReader <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/reactiveFileReader.html> to create auto-updating versions. This would mean even browsers that are already showing the old data, would automatically update themselves when new data arrives, without needing to reload. You can put the reactiveFileReaders above the shiny server function if the same data is to be shared by everyone.
>

messages.subject: Shiny as an executable
messages.subject_clean: Shiny as an executable
messages.body_plain:
I have a shiny app that we are using in my organization. The app has many R functions that are sourced in, html files, .css templates, etc, data sets, example files, and so on so this has become a large app.

My goal is to easily share the files needed to others so they can use them. I am doing this now by zipping the files, and users extract the program on their own computer and run the program.

This works, but has many limits. For example, we are in the initial phases and still working out bugs, so I am constantly emailing new updates and so on.

I have read all of the ways to share shiny and have used github and other web hosting services before to set up my app for users who do not have R and only use the app via the web.

I have no interest in building an R package. As a package maintainer now, the pain of building R packages is more than what I want to do for this current work.

Ideally, I would love for there to be a way to runUrl() on my .zip where I can save my zip file on a network drive that my coworkers have access to. I do not think this works based on the shiny help documentation, but am asking to see if anything has changed and does allow for this.

Also, wondering if any thought has been giving to make a shiny program a self contained executable such that users can simply launch the program from a desktop icon or something. I did this with python many years ago, it required that the user had python installed on their machine, but the program ran on top of that seamlessly.

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: suppress red error messages in shiny webpage
messages.subject_clean: suppress red error messages in shiny webpage
messages.body_plain:
That's a great point. I still would be wary of completely squelching even the fact that an error has occured, since that could lead your users to rely on erroneous values thinking they were correct. What if the specific error message is replaced by a generic error message?

On Thu, Feb 18, 2016 at 1:45 PM Benjamin Birnbaum <benjamin...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I share Lukáš's concern.  The reason I want to suppress error messages is for security, and changing the style of the error messages doesn't actually make them invisible to the client.  Lukáš did you find a solution?  It would be ideal if there was a "prod-mode" of shiny server that made sure no error text ever got to the user.
>
>
> On Tuesday, June 23, 2015 at 8:00:13 PM UTC-4, Dario Strbenac wrote:
> > You should use validate and need functions. For example, if you want to plot a data row from a matrix with one of its row names equal to the value stored in the variable featureName, the first lines of your reactive expression should be :

messages.subject: Re: Varying loading time
messages.subject_clean: Varying loading time
messages.body_plain:
When applications are not in use (have no connections), they go to sleep. The next time someone visits them, they will automatically be woken up (thats what is happening when you see "Please Wait").

You can adjust how long an idle application will wait before going to sleep by setting the "Instance Idle Timeout". Keep in mind, increasing this means you will consume active hours even when nobody is using your application. Any time the application is not sleeping is considered an active hour.

-Andy

Dnia 19.02.2016 o godz. 15:22 Andy Kipp <an...@rstudio.com> napisał(a):

When applications are not in use (have no connections), they go to sleep. The next time someone visits them, they will automatically be woken up (thats what is happening when you see "Please Wait").

You can adjust how long an idle application will wait before going to sleep by setting the "Instance Idle Timeout". Keep in mind, increasing this means you will consume active hours even when nobody is using your application. Any time the application is not sleeping is considered an active hour.

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
This is a performance/convenience related question .
I have 2500 weather data files. The user of my shiny app can select/view/plot etc any multiple of weather files. for eg view 4 out of 2500 weather files

Option 1:
Load all the 2500 data files as a list of dataframes
weather.data <- list("df1" = df1, "df2"= df2, ... "df2500" = df2500)
weather.data is now ~2GB in size according to Rstudio. I can saveRDS it and save it to file (~170MB) and later load it before shinyServer().
The user can then simply pick the dataset from the list. As the list is already loaded subsetting the list will be very fast for all the users.

Option 2:
Load just the dataset the user asked for
weather.data1, weather.data2,... weather.data2500
Each of these when saved to file are ~70KB. These are then loaded inside shinyServer().

Which of these are better if the shiny app is to be hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
For option2 will the user feel a delay while his specific data is loaded since it is loaded inside shinyServer()

Mike,

If you're connecting to a database over the internet, I recommend you use a TLS (secure) connection on your database. This isn't really a shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> specific issue, since the point is to protect your information once it leaves shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/> servers and travels to your database, you don't want nefarious 3rd party in the middle to snoop that data.

What type of database are you connecting to?

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
Hi

I want to make a simple interactive bubble chart with shiny and ggplot 2.  I have an example data frame 'dF'.   I want to plot 'dF$date' on the x axis and 'dF$score' on the y axis.

I want the user to be able to select the 'size' of the bubble and the 'group' of the bubble.

The code and sessionInfo() is below and I am attaching the app.r file too

I face errors when adjusting the 'sliderInput' and/or when selecting the 'selectInput'

For example:

When I have one selectInput value, ggplot  seems to make a plot
When I have two selectInput values, ggplot makes a plot but there are points missing.  In addition only some combinations of two inputs work.
When I select three or more selectInput values no plot is created with the following error
Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (1): size, colour, x, y

I think there may be a problem with my variable types and my aes() calls.

Any help on how to make this interactive bubble chart work correctly would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks In advance
Sanjeev

##############################################################################################################

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

dF<-data.frame(
  id=c("26807712", "26794930", "26518434","26847041","26504153", "26824982", "26773072", "26757162", "26810136", "26781275"),
  date=c("2016-01-26","2016-01-22","2016-01-15","2016-02-05","2015-12-19","2016-01-29","2016-01-16", "2016-01-12","2016-01-26", "2016-01-19"),
  score=c(1, 6.5, 3, 4, 2.5, 4, 5, 9, 3,4),
  rank=c(10, 15, 5, 6, 8, 14, 19, 2, 5, 7),
  class=c("OBS","RCT","GEN","META","RCT","DIA","OBS" ,"META","GEN","DIA"))

dF$date<-as.Date(dF$date)

print(str(dF))

ui<-fluidPage(

  titlePanel(title="Interactive Bubble Chart"),

  sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(
      ### Input for Impact
      sliderInput("impact","Choose an Impact", min=min(dF$rank), max=max(dF$rank), value=c(5,10)),

      ## Input for Method
      selectInput("method", "Choose a Methodology",choices=as.character(dF$class), multiple=T, selected = "OBS")

    ),

    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("plot"),
      textOutput("text1")

    )

  )

)

server<-function(input, output){

  subsetted <- reactive({
    dF %>%
      filter(rank >= input$impact[1] & rank <= input$impact[2]) %>%
      filter(class == input$method)

  })

 output$plot<-renderPlot({

    if (is.null(subsetted()))
      return(NULL)

    ggplot(subsetted(), aes(date,score)) +

      geom_point(aes(size=input$impact, colour=input$method)) +

      ylim(-1,10)

      })

  output$text1<-renderText({

    paste("You have selected this", input$method)

  })

}

shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server)

messages.subject: R/Shiny vs FileMaker (discussion about data visualization and reporting)
messages.subject_clean: R/Shiny vs FileMaker (discussion about data visualization and reporting)
messages.body_plain:
I work at a company that has about 20 years invested in FileMaker development. We're a marketing company in the tourism industry. We have very little automated reporting and no automated data visualization. I have experience with R and Shiny and would like to start using this experience to do analysis, create charts, and to automate reporting.

I'm looking for some good references that describe the advantages and disadvantages of these platforms:
- FileMaker (relational database with integrated forms, reporting, basic charts)
- R and any related products such as Shiny, R Markdown, RStudio Server, Shiny Server, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, etc

Here are some specific questions, but any information would be welcome, especially general arguments that can be presented to a non-technical board of directors.

- Which types of tasks/analysis should be done in our relational data base (FileMaker) and which are better done with R?
- What can be done with R that would be tedious or impossible with FileMaker?
- How are the graphics in R better than FileMaker (in my option, FileMaker charts are similar to Excel but perhaps less customizable)
- How can we best set up our infrastructure so that users aren’t overwhelmed with knowing when they should go to FileMaker to find what they’re looking for and when to look at a Shiny webpage? Should we imbed the Shiny page within a FileMaker database as a separate layout?

I'll be checking back to answer any follow-up questions.

> Hi all,
> Not sure if it has been identified before, most of the posts I've seen on shiny debugging have been pointed towards dumping variables to stderr file outputs, and I hadn't seen any way to debug things to console, so here's an attempt that seems to work for most cases. The main idea is to use console.table() for dataframes passed as JSON, text variables passed as text for console.log() and a way to group them together using console.group().  I'm sure there's quite a bit that can be improved and cleaned from here but it provides a quick way to see variable outputs to the console!
>
>
> ui.R:
>
> library(shiny)
> library(shinyjs)
>
> shinyUI(fluidPage(
>   useShinyjs(),
>   source("DebugMe.R", local = TRUE),
>   titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),
>   sidebarLayout(
>     sidebarPanel(
>       sliderInput("bins",
>                   "Number of bins:",
>                   min = 1,
>                   max = 50,
>                   value = 30)
>     ),
>     mainPanel(
>       plotOutput("distPlot")
>     )
>   )
> ))
>
> server.R
>
> library(shiny)
> library(shinyjs)
> library(jsonlite)
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>   output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
>     x    <- faithful[, 2]
>     js$logme("DebugTab","group")
>     js$logme(as.character(toJSON(head(iris))),"table")
>     js$logme(input$bins)
>     bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
>     hist(x, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white')
>   })
> })
>
>
> DebugMe.R
>
> jsCode <- "shinyjs.logme = function(params) {
>   var defaultParams = {
>     obj : null,
>     type : 'text'
>   };
>   params = shinyjs.getParams(params, defaultParams);
>
>   if (params.type == 'table'){
>     console.table(JSON.parse(params.obj))
>   } else if (params.type =='text') {
>     console.log(params.obj)
>   } else {
>     console.group(params.obj)
>   }
>
> }"
>
> extendShinyjs(text = jsCode)

messages.body_plain:
If you have three action buttons that are each going to have their own unique way of populating the same table, you can do that with a reactive values object plus observeEvent. In your server function:

rv <- reactiveValues(table = NULL)

observeEvent(input$goButtonb, {
  # Do some calculations...
  rv$table <- ...
})

observeEvent(input$goButtons, {
  # Do some calculations...
  rv$table <- ...
})

observeEvent(input$goButtona, {
  # Do some calculations...
  rv$table <- ...
})

output$inc <- renderTable({ rv$table })

Still, users are mistakenly clicking on the "GO" button twice and the whole computation is starting again.

Is there any easy way to disable the "GO" action button until the computation is finished?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Disable the action button until the computation is finished?
messages.subject_clean: Disable the action button until the computation is finished?
messages.body_plain:
shinyjs has the toggleState which will do what you want. I've had the same problem before, and I've noticed that most users can't spot the progress bars on top of the screen, so I ended up using a combo of toggleState (for things that get loaded to initialize a given selectize) and using 'shiny-busy' with a spinning logo in a conditional panel in your ui file to tell users to chill and stop the clicky-clicky... :)

conditionalPanel(condition="$('html').hasClass('shiny-busy')",
                               absolutePanel(top="25%", left ="25%",
                                             wellPanel(style="background-color:green; color:white",
                                                       draggable = TRUE,icon("refresh fa-spin fa-2x", lib="font-awesome"),
                                                       "Loading..."
                                             )
                               )
              )

> I am in the process of automating a computationally intensive process and have used the progress bars to indicate the status of the job.

>
> Is there any easy way to disable the "GO" action button until the computation is finished?

> Thanks.

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

r_colors <- rgb(t(col2rgb(colors()) / 255))

  leafletOutput("mymap"),

  actionButton("recalc", "New points")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  points <- eventReactive(input$recalc, {
    cbind(rnorm(40) * 2 + 13, rnorm(40) + 48)
  }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

  output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>%
      addProviderTiles("Stamen.TonerLite",

}

messages.body_plain:
Also posted on SF: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/35704056/shiny-rendertable-add-to-row

I have a dataframe that could look like this
> df
Product    noPat     Val  Tot TotVal
Product A  -318 -108.12 1356 461.04
Product C   403  544.05  462  623.7
Product D   -32  -39.68  529 655.96
Product B   N/A     N/A  N/A    N/A

I would like to add two multicolumns using the add.to.row argmument in the xtable function.
print(xtable(df, digits=2, caption=strCaption, label="Test_table"),
      size="footnotesize", #Change size; useful for bigger tables
      include.rownames=FALSE, #Don't print rownames
      caption.placement="top",
      hline.after=NULL, #We don't need hline; we use booktabs
      add.to.row = list(pos = list(-1,
                                   nrow(df)),
                        command = c(paste("\\hline \n",
                                          "& \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Growth} & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Total} \\\\ \n",
                                          "\\hline \n"),
                                    "\\hline \n")
      )
)

Which generates the desired latex output:
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\caption{test}
\label{Test_table}
\begingroup\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{lllll}
  \hline
 & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Growth} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Total} \\
 \hline
Product & noPat & Val & Tot & TotVal \\
 Product A & -318 & -108.12 & 1356 & 461.04 \\
  Product C & 403 & 544.05 & 462 & 623.7 \\
  Product D & -32 & -39.68 & 529 & 655.96 \\
  Product B & N/A & N/A & N/A & N/A \\
   \hline
\end{tabular}
\endgroup
\end{table}

Which is the format I want. I would like Shiny to output this, but Shiny just adds the add.to.row argument as text output just above the table.

My implementation in Shiny:

Server.R
output$tabletest <- renderTable({
        rows <<- nrow(df)
        xtable(df, digits=2)

      },

      caption = "Sample Data",
      caption.placement = getOption("xtable.caption.placement", "bottom"),
      caption.width = getOption("xtable.caption.width", NULL),
      include.rownames=getOption("xtable.include.rownames", FALSE), #Don't print rownames
      add.to.row = getOption("xtable.add.to.row",list(pos = list(-1,
                                   rows),
                        command = c(paste("\\hline \n",
                                          "& \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Growth} & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{Total} \\\\ \n",
                                          "\\hline \n"),
                                    "\\hline \n")))
      )

UI.R
tableOutput("tabletest")
